taxonomyNote: NatureServe treats C. pyrrhus as distinct from C. mitchellii of Baja California (Meik et al. 2015); other agency pages (CDFW) still use C. mitchellii for the same desert snakes, so this slug and speckled-rattlesnake may describe one U.S. population.
fieldMarks: Colour ranges from pale sandy gray to dark brown; the speckled pattern makes the diamond markings less distinct than on other rattlesnakes (NDOW).
Alternating light and dark tail rings are prominent (NDOW).
Medium-sized pit viper; NatureServe gives about 92-130 cm (NatureServe).
behavior: Ambush predator of small mammals, lizards and birds (NatureServe).
Inactive through cold winter months in sheltered crevices; females give birth to live young in late summer, typically 3-11 per litter (NDOW).
When inactive it shelters under rocks or bushes, in crevices, caves, abandoned mines, rodent burrows or woodrat nests (NatureServe).
habitat: Rugged, rocky terrain in the Mojave and Sonoran desert mountains; rarely on adjacent desert flats; primary habitat is rocky lower slopes and canyons, also seeps, springs and riparian areas (NatureServe).
range: Northern half of the Baja California Peninsula north into southern California, southern Nevada, western Arizona and southwestern Utah (NatureServe); in Nevada a small range in the southeast, overlapping the Panamint rattlesnake near Las Vegas (NDOW).
